newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs soar after better-than-expected 10-yr auction.
newsitem.headline: JGBs soar after better-than-expected 10-yr auction.

text.p: The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Tuesday's Tokyo session sharply higher after a better-than-expected 10-year JGB auction, traders said.
The December closed at its intraday high of 125.30, up from 124.65 on Monday.
"Following a better-than-expected auction, dealers rushed to cover short positions before the close," a brokerage house trader said.
The 2.8 percent 10-year JGB auction produced a lowest price of 100.30, the Ministry of Finance said.
Market participants had been expecting a lowest price of around 100.20 to 100.25, traders said.

"Prior to the auction, dealers set up short positions for hedging purposes, as this auction had been widely expected to produce a poor result. On the contrary, sales of the new JGBs are going fairly well despite a record low coupon of 2.8 percent," the brokerage house trader said.

With the auction out of the way, market players are now focusing on the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment, due to be released at 8.50 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT Tuesday).
Experts' average forecast for the tankan's headline diffusion index (DI) of major manufacturers' business sentiment was around minus three, compared with minus seven in the previous tankan.
Traders said the market had already factored in a modest improvement in the November DI and may be more interested in the DI forecast for March 1997.
"With the 10-year auction out of the way, JGBs could rise if the tankan figures come out weaker than expected," a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
In late morning trade, JGB futures were pushed higher by vague talk that some regional banks were facing financial problems.
In the Tokyo stock market, shares of some regional banks fell sharply.

Rumours of banks' financial difficulties are generally considered a bullish factor for JGBs, as they underscore the need for the central bank to maintain an easy credit policy to help banks clean up bad loans.
Early in the afternoon, there was also talk of some foreigners buying JGB futures, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.575 percent as of 4.20 p.m. (0720 GMT), down from 2.630 percent on Monday.
It was trading at around 2.600 percent before the results of the 10-year auction were announced at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT).
